   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function
   470	of the parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$.
   471	The lemma also establishes the time complexity of computing the {description} of
   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.
   474	
   475	
   476	
   477	\begin{lemma}[Complexity of the classical low-degree test]
   478	  \label{lem:ld-complexity}
   479	  Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$ denote a parameter tuple.
   480	  \begin{enumerate}
   481		\item The time complexity of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   482	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ is $\poly(m, d, k, \log q)$.
   483		\item The time complexity of evaluating marginals of the CL functions
   484	    $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$, and $L_\DLine$ at a given input point is $\poly(m, \log
   485	    q)$.
   486		\item The Turing machine description of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   487	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ can be computed from $\ldparams$ in $\polylog
   488	    (q,m,d,k)$ time.
   489	  \end{enumerate}
   490	\end{lemma}
   491	
   492	\begin{proof}
   493		Finite field arithmetic over $\F_q$ can be performed in time $\polylog q$, by
   494	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}.
   495		The most expensive step in $\decider^\ld$ is to evaluate a univariate
   496	  polynomial $f: \F_q \to \F_q^k$ at some point $t_u \in \F_q$ that corresponds
   497	  to a point $u \in \F_q^m$, which takes time $\poly(m,d,k,\log q)$.
   498	  The function $L_\Point$ is a projection onto $V_\xpt$, which takes time
   499	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ to compute (it just involves ``zeroing out'' the registers
   500	  outside of $V_\xpt$).
   501	  The functions $L_\ALine$ and $L_\DLine$ require computing a canonical linear
   502	  map, which requires performing Gaussian elimination and can be done in time
   503	  $\poly(m,\log q)$.
   504	
   505	  The Turing-machine description of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ can be
   506	  uniformly computed from the integers $(q,m,d,k)$ expressed in binary; the
   507	  complexity of computing the description comes from describing the parameter
   508	  tuple $\ldparams$, which takes time that is at most polynomial in the bit
   509	  length of $(q,m,d,k)$.
   510	\end{proof}

    37	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree polynomial classes]
    38		\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
    39		\uses{def:line, def:line-representative, def:polyfunc}
    40		Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
    41		$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
    42		$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
    43		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
    44		the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
    45		denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
    46		most $d$.
    47		% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
    48		% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
    49		% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
    50		% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
    51		% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
    52		% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
    53		% definition.
    54		For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
    55		by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
    56		question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
    57		point is the canonical representative of
    58		Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
    59		we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
    60		at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
    61		by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
    62		as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
    63		line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
    64		$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
    65		$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
    66		zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
    67		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
    68		\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
    69		every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
    70		unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
    71		so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
    72		function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
    73		operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
    74		$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
    75		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
    76		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
    77		$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
    78		rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
    79		evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
    80		obtained by adjoining the additional class
    81		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
    82		$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
    83		respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
    84		as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
    85		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
    86	\end{definition}

+/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
+descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
+the same effect as applying it once. -/
+theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
+    (v u : Fin m → K) :
+    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
+  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
+
+/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
+inductive LineKind where
+  | axis
+  | diagonal
+  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
+
+/-- A seed-bearing line description for `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
+
+An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
+stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
+Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
+appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
+corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
+inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
+  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
+      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
+  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
+      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
+      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
+      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
+  deriving DecidableEq
+
+/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
+def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
+  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
+  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
+
+/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
+def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
+  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
+  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
+
+/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
+def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
+  | .axis base _ _ => base
+  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
+
+/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
+Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
+not apply a second projection. -/
+def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
+    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
+  match line with
+  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
+  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction

+theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
+    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
+    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
+  cases line with
+  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
+  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
+
+/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
+noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
+    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
+  linePoints line.base line.direction
+
+/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
+most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
+abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
+
+/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
+def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
+    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
+  fun i =>
+    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
+
+/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
+and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
+the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
+def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
+    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
+  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
+    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
+
+/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
+when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
+completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
+noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
+    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
+  classical
+  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
+    some (Classical.choose h)
+  else none
+
+/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
+def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
+  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
+  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
+  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
+
+/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
+def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
+  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
+  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
+  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
+    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
+      intro j hj
+      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
+      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
+
+/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
+noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
+    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
+    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
+
+/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
+noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
+    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
+    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
+
+/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
+`def:line-point-dist`; paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
+noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
+    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
+    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
+
+/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
+theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
+    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
+theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
+    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
+theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
+    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
+  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
+    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
+    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:90-101`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`. -/
    20	def Strategy.IsProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=

    22	    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.B y)
    23	
    24	/-- Symmetric games from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    25	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
    26	The question and answer alphabets are each represented by a single shared type,
    27	matching the source notation. -/
    28	structure SymmetricGame where
    29	  Question : Type
    30	  Answer : Type
    31	  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
    32	  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
    33	  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
    34	  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
    35	  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
    36	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    37	  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)
    38	  decide : Question → Question → Answer → Answer → Bool
    39	  decide_symm : ∀ x y a b, decide x y a b = decide y x b a
    40	
    41	attribute [instance] SymmetricGame.questionFintype SymmetricGame.answerFintype
    42	  SymmetricGame.questionDecidableEq SymmetricGame.answerDecidableEq
    43	
    44	/-- Regard a symmetric game as a game with equal question and answer types;
    45	`def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    46	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
    47	def SymmetricGame.toGame (G : SymmetricGame) : Game where
    48	  QuestionA := G.Question
    49	  QuestionB := G.Question
    50	  AnswerA := G.Answer
    51	  AnswerB := G.Answer

    53	  μ_prob := G.μ_prob

    60	structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
    61	  ι : Type
    62	  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
    63	  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]
    64	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)
    65	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    66	  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
    67	  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι
    68	
    69	attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq
    70	
    71	/-- Regard a symmetric strategy as a strategy using the same local space and
    72	measurement family for both players; `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    73	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
    74	def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :
    75	    Strategy G.toGame where
    76	  ιA := S.ι
    77	  ιB := S.ι
    78	  ψ := S.ψ
    79	  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
    80	  A := S.M
    81	  B := S.M
    82	
    83	/-- Common-space commutation from `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
    84	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
    85	def IsCommutingOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    86	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    87	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
    88	    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
    90	    (B : Y → Measurement β ι) : Prop :=
    91	  ∀ x y, 0 < μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((B y).effect b)
    92	
    93	private def transportOp {d₁ d₂ : Type u} (h : d₁ = d₂) (M : Op d₂) : Op d₁ :=
    94	  h.symm ▸ M
    95	
    96	/-- Transported common-space form of `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
    97	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
    98	def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (hι : S.ιA = S.ιB) : Prop :=
    99	  ∀ x y, 0 < G.μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b,

   102	/-- Measurement consistency from `def:consistent-measurement`, blueprint
   103	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:152-161`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:144-160`. -/
   104	def Measurement.IsConsistentOn {α ι : Type*}

   106	    (M : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=

   109	
   110	/-- General strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
   111	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
   112	def IsConsistentStrategyOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
   113	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
   114	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   115	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   116	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : Y → Measurement β ι)
   117	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   118	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧

   123	def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
   124	    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=

   126	
   127	/-- The PCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,

   129	def Strategy.IsPCC {G : Game} {ι : Type*}

   133	    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)

   138	
   139	/-- The SPCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,
   140	paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
   141	def SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC {G : SymmetricGame}

   145	
   146	/-- Source symmetrization statement `lem:symmetric-strat`, blueprint

   148	The attainment defect is `rem:symmetric-strat-limit` and is tracked in
   149	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
   150	theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy (G : SymmetricGame) (ε : ℝ)
   151	    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : G.toGame.value = 1 - ε) :
   152	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧

   155	
   156	/-- Value-preserving formalization-only form of `lem:symmetric-strat` starting
   157	from a specified near-optimal strategy; blueprint
   158	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:116-135`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
   159	The source attainment distinction is tracked in

   161	theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy (G : SymmetricGame)

   165	  sorry
   166	
   167	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-! # Typed conditionally linear distributions

     8	uniform seed.

    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:typed-cl-functions` and `def:typed-cl-distributions` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:599-629`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-94`.
    15	-/

    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	/-- A typed family whose member at every type is `ell`-level conditionally
    22	linear. This is `def:typed-cl-functions`, blueprint
    23	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:599-604`, paper
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63`. -/
    25	def IsTypedCondLinearFamily (K T : Type*) [Field K]
    26	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    (ell : ℕ) (L : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    28	  ∀ t, IsCondLinear ell (L t)
    29	
    30	/-- The typed CL distribution: sample a type pair from the graph distribution,
    31	then bind it to the CL distribution selected by those two types. This is
    32	`def:typed-cl-distributions`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:624-629`, paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    34	noncomputable def typedCLDistribution {K T ι : Type*}
    35	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    36	    [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty)
    38	    (L R : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    39	    Distribution ((T × (ι → K)) × (T × (ι → K))) :=
    40	  Distribution.bind (graphDistribution E hE) fun uv =>
    41	    (clDistribution (L uv.1) (R uv.2)).map fun xy =>
    42	      ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))

    25	/-- Consistency bounds state-dependent distance, with the explicit factor

    28	theorem opFamilyDistSq_le_two_mul_consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    29	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    30	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if

    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.

    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}

   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}

   183	Recall that for a (pure) state $\ket{\psi}\in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$, the \emph{Schmidt rank} of $\ket{\psi}$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that 
   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]
   185	for some orthonormal families $\{\ket{u_i}\}\subset \mH_\alice$ and $\{\ket{v_i}\}\subset\mH_\bob$ and $\alpha_i>0$. The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}. The state $\ket{\psi}$ is called \emph{maximally entangled} if $\alpha_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots,k$.  
   186	
   187	
   188	\begin{definition}[Entanglement requirements of a game]
   189	  \label{def:ent}
   190		For all games $\game$ and $\nu \in [0, 1]$, let $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ denote the
   191	  minimum integer $d$ such that there exists a finite dimensional tensor product
   192	  strategy $\strategy$ that achieves success probability at least $\nu$ in the
   193	  game $\game$ with a state $\ket{\psi}$ whose Schmidt rank is at most $d$.
   194	  If there is no finite dimensional strategy that achieves success probability
   195	  $\nu$, then define $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ to be $\infty$.
   196	\end{definition}

   200	\begin{remark}
   201	  A strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for a symmetric game $\game =
   202	  (\cal{X}, \cal{X}, \cal{A}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ is called \emph{synchronous} if
   203	  it holds that for every $x\in \cal{X}$ and $a\neq b \in \cal{A}$, $\bra{\psi}
   204	  A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi} = 0$; in other words,
   205	  the players never return different answers when simultaneously asked the same
   206	  question.
   207	  As shown in~\cite{paulsen2016estimating} the condition for a
   208	  finite-dimensional strategy of being synchronous is equivalent to the
   209	  condition that it is projective, consistent, and moreover $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   210	  maximally entangled state.
   211	  (The equivalence is extended to infinite-dimensional strategies, as well as
   212	  correlations induced by limits of finite-dimensional strategies,
   213	  in~\cite{kim2018synchronous}.)
   214	\end{remark}
   215	\subsection{Distance measures}
   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)
   230	\end{definition}
   231	
   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}
   241	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}
   244	    = O(\delta)\;.\footnote{Here the use of the $O(\cdot)$ notation refers to the fact that the notation will often be used to measure consistency for \emph{famillies} of POVM and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n\in \mathbb{N}$, which will always be clear from context but omitted for legibility, see Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}. The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}
   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}
   249	
   250	Note that a consistent measurement on $\ket{\psi}$ according to
   251	Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same $\ket{\psi}$ and under
   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]
   255	because using that $\{M_a\}$ is a POVM there must be equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
   256	\[ 1 = \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\, \leq\, \Big(\sum_a \|\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)\Big(\sum_a \|M_a\otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)^{1/2} \,\leq\,1 \;.\]
   257	
   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.
   271	\end{definition}
   272	
   273	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]
   274	  \label{def:strategy-distance}
   275	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game
   276	  and let $\strategy = (\psi, A, B)$, $\strategy' = (\psi', A', B')$ be 
   277	  strategies for $\game$.
   278	  For $\delta\in[0,1]$ we say that \emph{$\strategy$ is $\delta$-close to
   279	    $\strategy'$} if the following conditions hold.
   280	  \begin{enumerate}
   281		\item The states $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\psi'}$ are states in the same
   282	    Hilbert space $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ and are $\delta$-close.
   283		\item For all $x \in \cal{X}, y \in \cal{Y}$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta
   284	    (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations
   285	    holding under the distribution $\mu$, and on either $\ket{\psi}$ or
   286	    $\ket{\psi'}$.
   287	  \end{enumerate}
   288	\end{definition}

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}
  1445	\end{theorem}
  1446	
  1447	We provide a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli} in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
  1448	
  1449	
  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.
  1456	By definition of normal form verifier, $\sampler$ is a sampler over $\F_2$, and
  1457	therefore it is natural to use a test for qubit Pauli measurements.
  1458	
  1459	Since we use field sizes $q$ that are powers of $2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary}
  1460	shows that the conclusions of \Cref{thm:pauli} can also be described in terms of
  1461	testing for maximally entangled states over qubits and qubit Pauli measurements.

  1488	
  1489	\begin{proof}
  1490	\Cref{lem:pauli-binary} implies that there are local isometries that map $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}$ to $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes M\log q}$, and map the generalized Pauli measurements $\tau^W_u$ to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^M \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}$ where $\kappa(u_i) = (u_{i1},\ldots,u_{i\log q})$. Combining this with the isometries guaranteed by \Cref{thm:pauli}, we obtain the statement of the Corollary.
  1491	\end{proof}
  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}
  1570	\begin{proof}

    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the

    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)

   111	
   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))

   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB

   157	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   158	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   159	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

   187	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]\label{def:state-distance}
   188		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n \in \N}$ be two families of states in the same space $\mathcal H$.    189		\[
   190			\lVert \ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n} \rVert^2 = O(\delta(n))\,.
   191		\]
   192		The dependence of the states and of $\delta$ on the indexing parameter $n$ is generally left implicit; we write, e.g., $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.

   201			A^x_a \ot \Id_B \simeq_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_a

   205			\E_{x \sim \mu} \sum_{a \ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^x_b \ket{\psi} = O(\delta)\,.

   599	The question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.

   605		Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \ge 0$. A \emph{$\mathcal T$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_t\}_{t \in \mathcal T}$ such that, for each $t \in \mathcal T$, $L_t$ is an $\ell$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.
   606	\end{definition}
   607	
   608	% Nonemptiness of the edge set is stated explicitly here: with E empty, m = k = 0 and the
   609	% normalization 1/(2m-k) below is undefined. The source
   610	% (references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82) leaves this boundary hypothesis implicit.
   611	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]\label{def:graph-distribution}
   612		Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and nonempty edge set $E$. Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
   613		\[
   614			\mu_G(u, v) =
   615			\begin{cases}
   616				1/(2m-k) & \text{if } \{u,v\} \in E\,,\\
   617				0 & \text{otherwise}\,.
   618			\end{cases}
   619		\]
   620		This is identical to the uniform distribution over ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ such that $\{u,v\} \in E$: each edge that is not a self-loop contributes two ordered pairs, and each self-loop contributes one, whence the normalization $2m-k$.
   621	\end{definition}

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

## 8. Concurrency

| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
|---|---|---|
| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |

The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
saves a write to a branch that has already moved.

Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.

`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
rewritten under it.

## 9. The findings ledger

`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
status signal; the REST `line` field lied.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`

`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;

the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
agreeing is intentional redundancy.

Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
not a verdict.

## 12. Deliberately not ported

Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".

* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
  One reviewer session; the cascade
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
  comes from a branch of this single repository.
* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
  allow-list only approximated.
* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).


## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)

A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:

1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   `moot: <reason>`);
2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.

**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.

**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.

read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

## 3. The merge gate

`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
